newsitem.title: INDIA: India accuses Pakistan of "unfriendly act".
newsitem.headline: India accuses Pakistan of "unfriendly act".

text.p: India accused Pakistan on Thursday of committing an "unfriendly act" by sending remote-controlled aircraft into Indian air space and summoned its ambassador to lodge a strong protest.
The Indian Defence Ministry said the Air Force was studying a video film of the small, pilotless aircraft which authorities said crossed into the western state of Gujarat from Pakistan on Wednesday.

The Air Force found pieces on Thursday of some of the missiles that were fired at the drone but no trace of the aircraft, the Defence Ministry said in a statement. It did not say how many aircraft nor what types of missiles were involved.
A ministry spokesman said the Foreign Ministry summoned Pakistan High Commissioner (ambassador) Riaz Khokhar.
"The Ministry of External Affairs has lodged a strong protest regarding these intrusions with the Pakistan high commissioner this evening," the Defence Ministry said.
"Pakistan authorities have been advised that India views this as an unfriendly act and such intrusions must cease immediately," it said.
Pakistan said no pilotless aircraft of its armed forces had crossed into Indian air space or had been fired on by the Indian Air Force.
"There is no truth in this allegation," a Foreign Ministry spokesman in Islamabad said. "There was no such plane and the incident has nothing to do with Pakistan."
It was not known if Wednesday's aircraft, called a Remotely Piloted Vehicle (RPV), had been hit, the Defence Ministry spokesman said.
"There have been some intrusions in the last couple of days in the Southwest Air Command region by remotely controlled, pilotless aircraft," the spokesman said.
"We believe this is the first occasion such aircraft have been involved in such incidents."

Indian forces in the region of the suspected intrusion near Bhuj airport, 300 km (190 miles) from the Gujarat state capital of Ahmedabad, had been put on alert and were searching for the aircraft, the defence spokesman said.
But ravines and sandy terrain in the region, located between Bombay and Karachi near the Arabian Sea, were hindering efforts to find debris, the ministry said.
The film of the pilotless aircraft was being examining at Air Force headquarters in New Delhi.
"This would help the Air Force in assessing the dimension, speed and other characteristics of the aircraft," the Defence Ministry said.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since they were carved out of British India in 1947.

Troops on both sides of the frontier regularly fire on each other in the disputed northern region of Kashmir, which was the cause of two of the three wars. The rest of the long border is closely monitored but generally peaceful.
The Hindu newspaper said the RPVs which crossed into Indian air space had sensors and night vision devices for surveillance.
